mechanism.summary: Represent transient RegExp matcher fan-out lists with one inline MatchState and spill to the existing heap-backed growth path only when an alternative or backtracking step produces multiple states.
mechanism.generality: The representation applies uniformly to the state and indexed-state collections returned by the general forward, reverse, group, lookaround, atom, quantifier, and simple-atom matcher paths. Selection depends only on the live number of semantic match states. It has no pattern-text, source-path, workload, input-length, iteration, checksum, or expected-result condition; zero and one-state results stay inline while arbitrary fan-out retains ordered heap growth.
semantic_risks: preserving exact ECMAScript leftmost-first order across alternatives plus greedy and lazy backtracking when an inline list spills
preserving independent MatchState capture ownership, branch cloning, capture clearing, and duplicate-state suppression without revisiting the rejected capture snapshot representation
preserving reverse matching, lookaround, Unicode advancement, zero-width-loop filtering, and unbounded explicit work stacks while only changing transient result-list storage
preserving every existing first-result and all-result boundary so the representation cannot prune states or turn a failure into a match
avoiding larger stack frames or spill bookkeeping that outweigh the removed singleton allocations on matcher and non-RegExp controls

profile_evidence.shared_cost: Of 2,925 main-thread samples, 811 are under PreparedRegexp::match_input. The hot capture-bearing route puts 212 samples in repeat_atom; 197 immediately enter Vec::from_iter and 192 continue through its iterator while nested match_pattern and match_atom calls repeatedly return empty or singleton Vec collections. The flat profile is led by allocator and free entry points. This state-list allocation is broader than capture payload cloning and distinct from the rejected first-continuation visitor because it changes neither MatchState contents nor continuation order.
